_comment: Verified display-number to bank-id map for the SHOSMED LF3 Chemistry Batch 2 review.
The supplied review carried NO bank ids; its Q1-Q60 were display numbers only, and it
warned explicitly against assuming a contiguous id run.
Each item was matched four ways before any edit: (1) a distinctive phrase from the
ORIGINAL stem, requiring exactly one match across all 485 chemistry records; (2) all
four ORIGINAL option texts; (3) the stored answer letter against the review's asserted
60-letter key block; (4) the A/B/C/D tally the review asserts (A=16, B=12, C=18, D=14).
All 60 matched uniquely on every check, and no stem phrase matched a second record, so
no duplicate resolution was needed. The resulting range turned out to be contiguous,
chem-63..chem-122, but that was a RESULT of the matching and not an assumption: the
harness and test re-derive the map from the before-fixture's original stems and options.
Coverage is computed from unique verified ids against the existing review ledger, not by
adding 60 to the prior count: none of these 60 ids appears in chemistry batch 1, so the
chemistry reviewed count rises from 60 to 120 of 485.
Conditional cleanup NOT needed: the review asked whether the stray 'Unanswered' label
before Q14 is stored in the stem. It is not. No record in the pack contains that string
in its stem, options or explanation, so it is a UI status label only and nothing was
removed on that account.
No record in the pack contains a table, matching the review's observation; none was added.
Heading policy: the review requires that every answer and distractor heading visibly
match its associated option, while also freezing option text outside the six specified
changes. Each edited item's headings are therefore set to its own option texts verbatim
(key heading = 'Correct Answer: <letter>. <option>', which is this pack's existing
convention; distractor heading = '<letter>. <option>:'). This propagates each item's own
option markup into its headings; normalising the ASCII markup inside option text itself
was out of scope. Q9 (chem-71) keeps one pre-existing divergence, heading 'CH4 (M=16)'
against option 'CH₄ (M=16)', because the review orders it kept byte-identical.
no_table_items: all 60; the pack has never carried a table and none was added

notes.what: The conditional 'Unanswered' stem cleanup was not needed.
notes.why: The review asked for it only if the label is actually stored. No record in the pack contains the string in its stem, options or explanation, so it is a UI status label.

notes.what: One heading still diverges from its option: heading 'CH4 (M=16)' against option 'CH₄ (M=16)'.
notes.why: The review's explicit instruction to keep Q9 byte-identical takes precedence over its general heading-agreement requirement. Repairing it would have edited an item the review ordered untouched.

notes.what: The existing sentence 'BaSO4 is so insoluble that it is used as a contrast agent in medical imaging of the gastrointestinal tract.' was kept verbatim.
notes.why: The review states that this sentence can stay and that no clinical guidance is needed. The surrounding prose now frames solubility as a guideline rather than literal zero solubility.

coverage.still_unreviewed_note: chem-19 (optical isomerism) and chem-61 (ideal gas, 300 K to 600 K at fixed volume) remain unreviewed inside the chem-1..chem-122 span; every other unreviewed chemistry id is chem-123 onward.
coverage.approval_status: Implementation checks passed. This pack is awaiting final scientific content approval, which is reported separately from software consistency.
